# OPFS VFS

> OPFS VFS is a persistent browser filesystem backed by the Origin Private File System. It maps logical files into a volume with a bounded set of native handles and offers synchronous I/O inside a dedicated worker.

The asynchronous worker client lets browser pages use the filesystem. Apps need HTTPS or localhost; APIs using SharedArrayBuffer also need cross-origin isolation. Browser storage belongs to an origin and is not a backup.

Disk buffering and balanced local durability are the defaults. Memory buffering also persists to OPFS; it is different from PGlite memory-only storage. Use explicit synchronization at important save points. Strict mode does not flush every disk-buffered write. A clean reopen benchmark does not establish crash or power-loss durability.

The React SDK preview provides volume providers and subscribed reads through `@opfs-vfs/react`. The `@opfs-vfs/effect` adapter provides scoped volumes, the FileSystem service, and change streams for `effect@4.0.0-rc.118`. PGlite and just-bash adapters are available. DuckDB and EdgeJS integrations are experimental and require matching custom runtime builds. Encryption with passkey-based access is a separate premium extension. The file-subscription plugin is available under the PolyForm Noncommercial License. It reports local logical changes and optional completed-file content. A premium cloud sync plugin is planned, but not yet available, to synchronize local volumes with backend cloud storage.

The repository uses the source-available PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0. Commercial use requires separate permission.

## Start here

- [Overview](https://opfs.dev/): Product benefits, integrations, and demos.
- [Motivation](https://opfs.dev/motivation/): The storage problem and design choices.
- [Documentation](https://opfs.dev/docs/): Guide index.
- [Getting started](https://opfs.dev/docs/getting-started/): Install, write, synchronize, and reopen a volume.
- [Browser setup](https://opfs.dev/docs/guides/browser-setup/): Secure context and isolation headers.
- [Volumes and lifecycle](https://opfs.dev/docs/concepts/): Volume names, buffering, and closing.

## File operations and tools

- [Files and directories](https://opfs.dev/docs/guides/files-and-directories/): Worker operations and truncation behavior.
- [Persistence and recovery](https://opfs.dev/docs/guides/persistence/): Save points, recovery logs, and buffer-mode changes.
- [Volume Explorer](https://opfs.dev/docs/guides/devtools/): Inspect, edit, and transfer volumes. Connections start read-only.
- [File preview extensions](https://opfs.dev/docs/guides/file-previews/): Trusted custom renderers and shared React previews.
- [API overview](https://opfs.dev/docs/reference/): Imports, options, inspection, and deletion.
- [Troubleshooting](https://opfs.dev/docs/troubleshooting/): Resolve errors without destructive recovery.

## Plugins

- [Plugins](https://opfs.dev/docs/plugins/): community subscriptions, separate premium encryption, and planned premium cloud sync.
- [File subscriptions](https://opfs.dev/docs/plugins/subscriptions/): npm installation, custom workers, filtering, content, and resubscribe/rescan recovery.

## Choose an API

- [TypeScript](https://opfs.dev/docs/getting-started/): Create a volume and read or write files.
- [React SDK preview](https://opfs.dev/docs/react/): Connect components to a volume with providers and subscribed reads.
- [React API reference](https://opfs.dev/docs/react/reference/): Providers, resource hooks, and lifecycle commands.
- [React demo](https://opfs.dev/demos/react/): File inbox and todo lists using dedicated workers.
- [Effect v4 adapter](https://opfs.dev/docs/effect/): Scoped volumes, the FileSystem service, and change streams. Requires `effect@4.0.0-rc.118`.

## Integrations

- [PGlite](https://opfs.dev/docs/integrations/pglite/): PostgreSQL storage and synchronization settings.
- [just-bash](https://opfs.dev/docs/integrations/just-bash/): Shell access to workspace files.
- [DuckDB](https://opfs.dev/docs/integrations/duckdb/): Experimental adapter and compatible engine downloads.
- [EdgeJS](https://opfs.dev/docs/integrations/edgejs/): Experimental live file access and compatible host downloads.

## Benchmarks

- [Published results](https://opfs.dev/benchmarks/): Device-specific measurements and raw exports. Mac and iPhone collections use different protocols; compare their settings before interpreting rankings.
- [Methodology](https://opfs.dev/benchmarks/methodology/): Timing boundaries, correctness checks, and collection limits.
- [Storage and durability](https://opfs.dev/benchmarks/storage/): Backends, buffering, flush policies, and handle usage.
- [PGlite runner](https://opfs.dev/benchmarks/run/): Run SQL workloads on the current device.
- [Filesystem runner](https://opfs.dev/benchmarks/filesystem/): Measure VFS file operations.
- [Collection](https://opfs.dev/benchmarks/collect/): Download repeatable result bundles. Nothing is uploaded automatically.

## Optional

- [Demos](https://opfs.dev/demos/): Interactive examples. Storage and model operations require a browser.
- [Local AI](https://opfs.dev/demos/ai/): Gemma with a browser-local workspace, an explicit model download, and WebGPU requirements.
- [Licensing](https://opfs.dev/licensing/): Full PolyForm Noncommercial license.
- [Changelog](https://opfs.dev/changelog/): Versioned package changes.
- [Sitemap](https://opfs.dev/sitemap/): All public pages.
